 Maui News 11.2% of Hawaiʻi residents rely on SNAP benefits as payouts drop, cuts loom
 November 17, 2026, 8:00 AM HST --> Play Listen to this Article 
 4 minutes Loading Audio... Article will play after ad... Playing in :00 A A A 
 An estimated 11.2% of Hawai ʻ i residents rely on Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program ( SNAP) benefits  as the average monthly benefit drops to $189 nationwide, squeezing household budgets ahead of the holidays. 
 The data was compiled by Trace One, a global provider of AI-native Product Lifecycle Management and regulatory compliance software for the food & beverage, cosmetics and personal care, and specialty chemical industries. Trace One mapped FY  2026 SNAP participation  across all 50 states in a new report. 
 Which States Have the Highest SNAP Participation Rates? 
 With one in five residents enrolled, New Mexico leads the country in SNAP participation 
 Source: Trace One analysis of USDA and Census data
 New Mexico has the highest share of residents receiving food assistance in the country at 20.9%—well above its 15.5% poverty rate. Other Western states with relatively high SNAP participation include Oregon (16.8%) and Nevada (12.6%), despite both having below-average poverty rates. Meanwhile, Utah (4.4%) and Wyoming (4.2%) have the lowest participation rates in the country.
 While SNAP participation broadly tracks poverty levels, state policies play a crucial role in shaping enrollment. More inclusive eligibility rules and outreach efforts can increase access, while stricter policies may limit participation even in high-need areas.
 Here is a summary of the data for Hawaii:
 SNAP participation reliance ranking:  #19
 Share of individuals receiving SNAP benefits:  11.2%
 Share of households receiving SNAP benefits:  16.1%
 Average monthly SNAP benefit per individual:  $325.11
 Average monthly SNAP benefit per household:  $649.43
 Total individuals receiving SNAP benefits:  160,775
 Total households receiving SNAP benefits:  80,486
 Average monthly SNAP benefits received:  $52,269,991
 Poverty rate:  9.3%
 For reference, here are the statistics for the entire United States:
 Share of individuals receiving SNAP benefits:  11.1%
 Share of households receiving SNAP benefits:  15.4%
 Average monthly SNAP benefit per individual:  $189.00
 Average monthly SNAP benefit per household:  $348.53
 Total individuals receiving SNAP benefits:  38,035,408
 Total households receiving SNAP benefits:  20,625,982
 Average monthly SNAP benefits received:  $7,188,688,123
 Poverty rate:  11.8%
 Key Takeaways for  Hawaiʻi 
 SNAP participation has fallen from its pandemic-era highs.  In fiscal year 2026, 38 million Americans—11.1% of the US population—received food assistance, down from 41.7 million in fiscal year 2024, and well below the all-time high of 47.6 million in 2013.
 SNAP participation in Hawaiʻi.  In Hawaiʻi specifically, 160,775 residents currently receive SNAP benefits—a figure threatened by recently proposed changes to the program.
 The purchasing power of food assistance has significantly diminished in recent years.  The average monthly benefit in the US has dropped to $189, a steep decline from the inflation-adjusted peak of nearly $263 in 2021.
 Monthly SNAP benefits in Hawaiʻi.  In Hawaiʻi, the average monthly benefit is $325.11.
 2026 has brought significant shifts to the SNAP program including:
 Stricter Work Requirements (Enacted):  Able-bodied adults without dependents nationwide must now meet expanded work or volunteer mandates to keep benefits.
 Federal Cost-Shifting (Enacted):  Reduced federal cost-sharing is forcing state and local governments to cover a larger share of program funding. Combined with work rules, an estimated 5.5 million Americans have lost SNAP over the past year.
 New Proposed Rule on Automatic Eligibility (Open for Comment):  Last week, the USDA proposed ending automatic SNAP qualification for recipients of Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF). Public comments are open until December. If finalized, it would take effect in roughly two years and could cut more than 6 million people from SNAP by 2029.
 To understand how these shifts are impacting different regions and demographics, Trace One’s analysis breaks down enrollment rates, monthly benefit values, and recipient demographics in all 50 states.
 How Many Americans Benefit from SNAP? 
 More than 38 million people—one in nine people nationwide—rely on SNAP food assistance 
 Source: Trace One analysis of USDA data
 As of fiscal year 2026, participation has receded from its pandemic-era highs. Today, more than 38 million Americans—11.1% of the U.S. population—receive SNAP benefits, with the program’s total monthly cost falling to $7.2 billion. Participants now receive an average monthly benefit of $189, a steep decline from the 2021 pandemic peak when the average monthly benefit reached nearly $263 in inflation-adjusted dollars.
 This sharp reduction in SNAP purchasing power is squeezing household budgets just as global disruptions drive up the  cost of groceries . Elevated fuel prices and new  trade tariffs  have significantly increased supply chain and ingredient costs for US food and beverage manufacturers. As manufacturers shuffle suppliers,  reformulate their products , and ultimately have to pass these higher production expenses downstream, the resulting price hikes hit grocery shelves quickly, directly eroding the diminished purchasing power of SNAP recipients at the checkout line.
 “When an ingredient costs more, a food manufacturer has three choices: raise the price, shrink the pack, or change the recipe. For the 38 million Americans on SNAP, every one of those choices shows up at the checkout,” said Saïda Aït, VP of Global Marketing at Trace One.
 What Are the Demographics of SNAP Recipients? 
 SNAP benefits are distributed across all ages, sexes, and races 
 Source: Trace One analysis of US Census Bureau data
 Children make up the largest share of SNAP recipients, with 32.1% of participants under the age of 18. Adults between the ages of 30 and 49 account for 25.2%, while those aged 18 to 29 make up 14.8%. Older adults comprise a smaller share of the SNAP program, with 14.9% of recipients between 50 and 64 years old and 13.0% aged 65 or older.
 Women represent a slight majority of SNAP recipients, accounting for 54%, compared to 46% who are men. Women are more likely to be in poverty than men and also more likely to have children in their household, increasing the likelihood of SNAP eligibility. Racial and ethnic diversity among recipients is also notable. 
 Asian or Pacific Islanders (non-Hispanic) comprise 5.3% of SNAP recipients, a rate slightly below their overall population share.
 Methodology 
 Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participation and benefits. Data sources include the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) SNAP Data Tables, the US Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) 1-Year Estimates, the US Census Bureau Families and Living Arrangements, and the US Bureau of Economic Analysis Personal Income and Outlays.
